_comment: B09 super jump: direct frontier of the power-flags word. Regenerate: tools/phase4_b09_frontier.py
target_is: u16 power-flags word; bit 0x20 = super jump. A FIELD of the player record at 0x800A6500 + 0x90 -- which is why a materialisation census of the field address is the wrong instrument here.
independent_reproduction: Canon derived 26 writers from the ori/andi immediates at each site. This derives the writer set from DATAFLOW over the repaired function list and gets 26. Two methods, same number.
readers_are_new: Canon documented writers only; the 54 readers here have not previously been enumerated for this row.

residual.note: Not yet classified. B06 classified its 251 into 12 domains with a proof per site; B09 has had no equivalent pass. This is the work item 2 still needs, and it is NOT claimed here.

finding: Both long-suspect PCs are confirmed WRITERS and both are WHOLESALE OVERWRITES of the entire flags word -- 0x8004867C stores immediate 1, 0x800486BC stores zero -- not read-modify-write masks. So if either is reachable after acquisition it definitively clears bit 0x20. The roadmap called them 'structural overwrite sites, not proven post-acquisition clears'; the overwrite half is now proven and the open question is purely REACHABILITY.
next_experiment: Arm an execTrace range watch over both PCs during a movie in which super jump is acquired and the level is played to exit. If neither fires post-acquisition, that is the reset/persistence law the row needs; if one does, the observed law 'lasts for the rest of the level' is wrong.
